rules.label: Invoice_Loader_updsvc
rules.text:
rule Invoice_Loader_updsvc
{{
  meta:
    description = "Invoice lure that drops updsvc"
  strings:
    $a = "cdn-update" nocase
    $b = "updsvc.exe" wide ascii
    $c = "UpdateService" wide ascii
  condition:
    2 of them
}}

brief.situation: You are a security analyst at Tallis Freight, a fictional logistics firm. At 09:00 an accounts payable clerk reports that an invoice attachment 'did nothing' when she opened it at 08:52 on WS-114. The mail gateway shows the same message went to six people. You have the attachment in the malware lab.
handover: The lab has an isolated sandbox with no route to production; EDR can isolate any workstation; you can change proxy and firewall blocks and deploy detection rules.
This is your own organization's incident: defensive work only. The report shows behavior in words, every address and domain is defanged or from documentation ranges, and nothing in it can be run.
howItWorks: Each task takes time: choose it, then let it finish, which moves the clock. The attacker keeps working on the same clock.
The report fills in as you analyze: static findings, the process tree, network calls, then your indicators and rules, and the hosts in scope.
When you close the incident you write the report and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the malware analysis report: what the sample does and how you know, how you found and contained every infected host, and which detections you deployed and why.

parts.label: Static and dynamic findings
parts.criteria: Static: macro document with obfuscated auto-open code and embedded strings; dynamic (in an isolated sandbox, not production): Word starts PowerShell, a second stage, updsvc.exe with a Run key (persistence), a 60-second beacon; separates the benign update check from the malicious traffic.
parts.modelAnswer: Static analysis showed an auto-open macro with a defanged download URL and the dropped file name; detonation in the isolated sandbox showed Word starting PowerShell, the s.dat download, updsvc.exe persisting through a Run key and a beacon to 198.51.100.23. The update.example.com call was the sandbox image's own.

parts.label: Scope and containment
parts.criteria: Uses the indicators to hunt across the fleet and finds the second host; isolates both and blocks the domain and addresses; images before rebuilding and rebuilds rather than deleting files.
parts.modelAnswer: The fleet search found WS-131 beaconing too. I isolated both, blocked the domain and both addresses, captured memory and disk, then rebuilt from the gold image, because deleting the file leaves whatever the second stage changed.

parts.label: Detections
parts.criteria: A YARA rule from strings unique to the family and a Sigma rule for Word starting PowerShell, both tested against known-good data before deployment; a broad rule rejected as noisy; indicators shared.
parts.modelAnswer: YARA on the family's own strings (2 of 3) and Sigma on Word starting PowerShell, both tested with no false positives in the goodware set, then deployed; indicators shared with the ISAC.

expertPath.text: Isolate WS-114; static analysis of the attachment.
Extract indicators; hunt the fleet: WS-131; isolate it; block the domain and addresses; detonate in the sandbox.
YARA from the family's strings and Sigma for Word starting PowerShell; test against known-good data; deploy; share indicators.
Memory and disk images, then rebuild both hosts; a full report.

contained.headline: Good: analyzed safely, scoped, detected
contained.body: The sandbox showed the chain; the indicators found the second host; tested, specific rules will catch the next one; rebuilding beats deleting.

gaps.headline: Contained, with gaps
gaps.body: A rule that fires on every macro document is noise; deleting a dropped file is not eradication; image before you rebuild.

selfInfected.headline: Never on production
selfInfected.body: Dynamic analysis belongs on an isolated test system (NIST SP 800-83 4.2.4), never a corporate machine.

spread.headline: Scope before you rest
spread.body: Six people got the message. The indicators from the analysis were the way to find the second host before its second stage.

leftOpen.headline: Not contained
leftOpen.body: Every host that ran the sample needs isolation, a block on its command channel and a rebuild before the incident closes.

time_up.headline: No report
time_up.body: Close the incident and write the report before the shift ends.

scoring.modelReasoning: Static: macro downloader. Dynamic in the isolated sandbox: Word to PowerShell to updsvc.exe with a Run key and a 60-second beacon; the update check was benign. Hunt with the indicators: WS-131; isolate both and block the domain and addresses; YARA on the family's strings and Sigma on the chain, tested then deployed; indicators shared; image then rebuild.
